dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:2801.text: To injure. From 刃 and 一.

shuowen:2802.text: A weapon worn by a person. From 刃; 僉 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2803.text: Skillful cutting. From 刀; 丯 supplies the sound. All graphs in this category contain 㓞.

shuowen:2804.text: 齘𠜵: to scrape. From 㓞; 夬 supplies the sound. Another explanation: to score something hard.

shuowen:2805.text: To carve. From 㓞 and 木.

shuowen:2806.text: Plants scattered in disorder. It depicts plants growing chaotically. All graphs in this category contain 丯. Pronounced like 介.

shuowen:2807.text: The expression 枝𠲱, apparently branching or interlaced growth. From 丯; 各 supplies the sound. [The descriptive sense is uncertain.]

shuowen:2808.text: A curved wooden hand-plowing implement. From 木 pushing aside 丯. Anciently Chui made 耒 and 㭒 to aid the people. All graphs in this category contain 耒.

shuowen:2809.text: To plow. From 耒; 井 supplies the sound. Another explanation: ancient well-fields.

shuowen:2810.text: A plow five inches wide is one 伐; two 伐 make an 耦. From 耒; 禺 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2811.text: The emperor's personally tilled thousand mu. Anciently employing the people was like borrowing, hence called 耤. From 耒; 昔 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2812.text: An implement described as 冊又 (Duan's commentary has 卌㕚), usable for raking wheat, used in Henei. From 耒; 圭 supplies the sound. [The recorded description is difficult.]

shuowen:2813.text: To remove weeds between seedlings. From 耒; 員 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2814.text: The Shang assessed seven in seventy under the 耡 system; 耡 is a labor-service levy. From 耒; 助 supplies the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “By promoting 耡, benefit the people.”

shuowen:2815.text: An animal's horn. A pictograph; its form resembles 刀 and 魚. All graphs in this category contain 角.

shuowen:2816.text: The appearance of waving horns. From 角; 雚 supplies the sound. Liang's 𨻳 county has a 䚭 station. Also pronounced like 𦄑.

shuowen:2817.text: A horn. From 角; 樂 supplies the sound. Zhangye has Lude county.

shuowen:2818.text: The bone within a horn. From 角; 思 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2819.text: A curved horn. From 角; 𢍏 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2820.text: A curved horn. From 角; 兒 supplies the sound. Xihe has Nishi county.

shuowen:2821.text: One horn pointing upward. From 角; 㓞 supplies the sound. The Changes says: “Its ox has an upturned horn.”

shuowen:2822.text: A tilted horn. From 角; 虒 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2823.text: One horn pointing down and one up. From 角; 奇 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2824.text: The appearance of a horn. From 角; 丩 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “The rhinoceros-horn cup curves upward.”

shuowen:2825.text: A horn curved in the middle. From 角; 畏 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2826.text: The appearance of a long horn. From 角; 爿 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2827.text: A horn striking and springing against something. From 角; 厥 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2828.text: To butt against. From 角; 蜀 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2829.text: Ease in lowering and raising horns. From 羊, 牛 and 角. The Odes says: “Supple is the horn bow.”

shuowen:2830.text: To raise the horns. From 角; 公 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2831.text: To work horn. From 角; abbreviated 學 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2832.text: When cattle butt, a large wooden crosspiece is fastened across their horns. From 角 and 大; 行 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “Set their nose-clamps and horn-crosspieces.”

shuowen:2833.text: 角𧤗, a beast resembling a pig whose horns are good for bows, found in the Hu kingdom Xiuduo. From 角; 耑 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2834.text: 觰拏, a beast. From 角; 者 supplies the sound. Another explanation: broad below.

shuowen:2835.text: Sheep's horns of unequal length. From 角; 危 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2836.text: A female 牂 sheep that grows horns. From 角; 圭 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2837.text: A name for bony horns. From 角; 各 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2838.text: The horn-like tufts on a 鴟舊 bird's head. Another explanation: 觜觿. From 角; 此 supplies the sound. [The alternate term is unexplained.]

shuowen:2839.text: To split. From 刀 splitting 牛角, an ox's horn. Another explanation: 解𢊁, a beast.

shuowen:2840.text: A horn ornament worn at the belt, with a sharp tip that can undo knots. From 角; 巂 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “The boy wears a 觿.”

shuowen:2841.text: A rhinoceros or ox horn from which one can drink. From 角; 黃 supplies the sound. Its shape is 觵觵, hence its name. [The descriptive repetition is not further explained.]

shuowen:2842.text: A horn cup for the district drinking rite. The Rites says: “One person washes and raises the 觶.” It holds four sheng. From 角; 單 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2843.text: A small 觶 cup. From 角; 旦 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2844.text: A 觶 when full is called 觴; empty, 觶. From 角; abbreviated 𥏻 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2845.text: A cup for the district drinking rite. Another explanation: a drinking cup holding three sheng is called 觚. From 角; 瓜 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2846.text: A horn spoon. From 角; 亘 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 讙.

shuowen:2847.text: A horn fitting at the end of a staff. From 角; 敫 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2848.text: A ring with a tongue. From 角; 敻 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2849.text: To tune or adjust a bow. From 角; abbreviated 弱 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2850.text: An implement for retrieving the cord when shooting birds with corded arrows. From 角; 發 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2851.text: An implement for retrieving a shooting cord. From 角; 酋 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 鰌.

shuowen:2852.text: To hold drinking vessels, 觵 and 卮. Another explanation: shooting equipment. From 角; 㱿 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 斛.

shuowen:2853.text: The horn called 屠𧥑, blown by Qiang people to frighten horses. From 角; 𢨋 supplies the sound. 𢨋 is the ancient form of 誖.

shuowen:2854.text: A plant that grows in winter. A pictograph; the hanging parts are the sheaths. All graphs in this category contain 竹.

shuowen:2855.text: An arrow. From 竹; 前 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2856.text: The bamboo 箘簬. From 竹; 囷 supplies the sound. Another explanation: a gaming piece.

shuowen:2857.text: The bamboo 箘簬. From 竹; 路 supplies the sound. The Book of Xia says: “箘, 簬 and 楛.”

shuowen:2858.text: A kind of arrow bamboo; small bamboo. From 竹; 攸 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2859.text: Large bamboo. From 竹; 湯 supplies the sound. The Book of Xia says: “瑤, 琨, 筱 and 簜.” 簜 can make shafts; 筱 can make arrows.

shuowen:2860.text: A bamboo. From 竹; 微 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2861.text: The embryo of bamboo, a shoot. From 竹; 旬 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2862.text: A bamboo sprout. From 竹; 怠 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2863.text: Bamboo sheath. From 竹; 咅 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2864.text: In Chu, bamboo's skin is called 箬. From 竹; 若 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2865.text: A bamboo joint. From 竹; 即 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2866.text: Split bamboo skin. From 竹; 余 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 絮.

shuowen:2867.text: Split bamboo skin, 筡. From 竹; 𦤝 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2868.text: The skin of bamboo. From 竹; 民 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2869.text: The inside of bamboo. From 竹; 本 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2870.text: The appearance of bamboo. From 竹; 翁 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2871.text: Uneven. From 竹; 𠻝 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2872.text: Drawn-out writing. From 竹; 彖 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2873.text: To read writing. From 竹; 㩅 supplies the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says “the diviner Zhou.”

shuowen:2874.text: A written text. Another explanation: west of the pass, a board is called 篇. From 竹; 扁 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2875.text: A register or written record. From 竹; 𦔡 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2876.text: A bamboo field. From 竹; 皇 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2877.text: Split bamboo with its joints not yet removed is called 䉃. From 竹; 將 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2878.text: The bamboo writing tablet 籥. From 竹; 枼 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2879.text: A bamboo tablet used by children learning to write. From 竹; 龠 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2880.text: The sound of bamboo. From 竹; 劉 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2881.text: A writing tablet. From 竹; 閒 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2882.text: Bamboo arranged in rows. From 竹; 亢 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2883.text: The object 㒼爰, apparently a bamboo basket or container. From 竹; 部 supplies the sound. [The rare gloss is unresolved.]

shuowen:2884.text: To make bamboo slips even. From 竹 and 寺; 寺 expresses the graded equality of government offices.

shuowen:2885.text: A law or model. From 竹, because bamboo is used for written slips; 氾 supplies the sound. Ancient law had punishments written on bamboo.

shuowen:2886.text: Writing that labels or marks. From 竹; 戔 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2887.text: A token of trust. Under Han regulations, made of bamboo, six inches long, split into matching halves. From 竹; 付 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2888.text: Using milfoil stalks for hexagrams of the Changes. From 竹 and 𢍮; 𢍮 is the ancient form of 巫.

shuowen:2889.text: A hairpin. From 竹; 幵 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2890.text: A fine comb for removing nits. From 竹; 𦣞 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2891.text: That which gathers silk. From 竹; 蒦 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2892.text: A tube used in winding silk. From 竹; 廷 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2893.text: The silk-winding tube 筟. From 竹; 完 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2894.text: The silk-winding tube 筳. From 竹; 孚 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 彄, the prince of Lu in the Spring and Autumn.

shuowen:2895.text: Pressed tightly, situated beneath roof tiles and above the rafters. From 竹; 乍 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2896.text: A hall's curtain or screen. From 竹; 廉 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2897.text: The slats of a bed. From 竹; 責 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2898.text: The slatted base of a bed. From 竹; 𠂔 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2899.text: A bamboo mat. From 竹; 延 supplies the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Measure the hall by 筵.” A 筵 is one zhang.

shuowen:2900.text: A bamboo mat. From 竹; 𪉷 supplies the sound.
